HSTU already provides a suitable mechanism: SiLU pointwise attention, learned relative position/time bias, and multiplicative gating. Its 2024 paper supports relative attention bias as a useful inductive bias, but does not establish that stronger recency weighting always improves recommendation. Without timestamps, relative interaction distance remains available; elapsed-time decay cannot be reconstructed from sequence order. [HSTU, ICML 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3)

Recent work strengthens the motivation for testing temporal weighting. FuXi-β (2025) introduces functional relative attention bias and reports that query–key attention can hurt performance in its experiments; replacing HSTU with its attention-free architecture would exceed the required family constraint. HyTRec (2026 preprint) explicitly separates stable preferences from recent intent and introduces a temporal-aware update mechanism to suppress historical noise, with reported gains on ultra-long industrial sequences. These results motivate an experiment, but do not establish gains on the four Amazon categories. [FuXi-β](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10615), [HyTRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.18283)

A compatible hypothesis is to retain HSTU’s backbone and add a jointly learned, per-head relative-position decay or content-conditioned recency gate inside its causal attention. Compare against the corrected baseline using macro validation HR@10; retain one jointly trained checkpoint per category. Here “causal” means blocking future interactions, not identifying causal intent. Sequence-only recency measures interaction distance, and neither purchase order nor timing establishes fulfilled needs.
